deep.reconstruction:
This page continues the lecture notes of 15.11.66, the 'laïus' that became Grothendieck's IHES talk 'Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes', written up by Coates and Jussila in Dix exposés, 1968.

The previous page set up the situation. Algebraic de Rham cohomology H_DR(X) = H^*(X, Ω^•_X) works over any base, and relatively as H_DR(X/S) = H^*(X, Ω^•_{X/S}) and R f_* Ω^•_{X/S}. But it needs smoothness. What is wanted is a p-adic cohomology for varieties in characteristic p, playing the role of ℓ-adic cohomology for ℓ ≠ p.

On this page Grothendieck restates the Monsky–Washnitzer (W-M) idea:
- Take X_0 smooth over a perfect field k, and a smooth lift X over S = Spec W(k).
- The cohomology H^*_DR(X/S) should, up to canonical isomorphism, not depend on the choice of the lift X of X_0.
- It would therefore be an invariant intrinsically attached to X_0, and could serve by definition as the sought 'p-adic' cohomology of X_0.

Remark a): the construction should still work, with modifications, when X_0 lifts only to a formal scheme smooth over S (a smooth formal lift over Spf W).

Remark b): from the published W-M text one might think that only H^i_DR(X/S) ⊗_W K (K the fraction field of W) has this invariance property. Moreover, W-M treat the construction and the invariance only for X_0 affine, using weakly complete (dagger) liftings, which resemble Tate rigid-analytic varieties (next page). Grothendieck is implicitly claiming more: invariance already integrally, over W, and for global, non-affine X_0.

The next page reports that Washnitzer, orally, had obtained the global integral invariants by working with de Rham complexes of liftings over the W_n, and had confirmed Grothendieck's assertions. It also adds remark c): via comparison theorems, when X_0 lifts to X smooth over S, this cohomology gives the correct Betti numbers (those of the generic fibre).

In modern terms this is exactly the motivating statement of crystalline cohomology: for X proper and smooth over W lifting X_0, there is a canonical isomorphism H^*_cris(X_0/W) ≅ H^*_DR(X/W), so H_DR(X/W) is independent of the lift integrally. This was carried out by Grothendieck in the 1966/68 exposé and by Berthelot in his thesis (1974), and later by Berthelot–Ogus. Remark a) corresponds to using formal lifts (formal schemes over Spf W) in the crystalline / Berthelot–Ogus framework.
errors: No real mathematical error. The independence claim implicitly needs properness, or a weak-completion (Monsky–Washnitzer) device in the non-proper case: for affine X_0, the algebraic de Rham cohomology of a smooth affine lift does depend on the lift. Grothendieck flags this indirectly by noting that W-M treat only the affine case. The integral (over W, not just K) canonical independence for proper smooth lifts is correct and was later proved via crystalline cohomology.
The machine transcription garbles the key sentence; see the transcription corrections.

ideas.what: De Rham cohomology of a smooth (proper) lift over W is, up to canonical isomorphism, independent of the lift, hence an intrinsic p-adic cohomology of X_0.
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (idea, 1966), Berthelot (1974), with Monsky–Washnitzer as precursor
ideas.where_published: Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes, in Dix exposés sur la cohomologie des schémas (1968)

ideas.what: Extending the construction to X_0 that lift only formally (smooth formal scheme over Spf W).
ideas.modern_name: formal lifts in crystalline / Berthelot–Ogus theory
ideas.where_published: Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes (1968)

ideas.what: Critique that Monsky–Washnitzer only treat affine X_0 and only rational (⊗K) invariance; claim that invariance holds integrally and globally.
ideas.modern_name: integral p-adic cohomology vs Monsky–Washnitzer / rigid cohomology
ideas.where_published: Dix exposés (1968), introduction to the crystals exposé

deep.surprise_reason: These are draft lecture notes for the well-known 1966 IHES talk that introduced crystalline cohomology. The content matches the published exposé. The only extra is minor historical colour (Grothendieck's reading of Monsky–Washnitzer and Washnitzer's oral communication on the next page).
transcription_corrections: Lines 3–4: 'ne dépend que de deux des relèvements X de X_0' should read approximately 'ne dépend pas du (choix du) relèvement X de X_0'.
End of the first paragraph: 'la cohomologie "p-adique" de [?]' is probably 'la cohomologie "p-adique" cherchée'.
Margin note: 'Some properties of formal schemes 63/64 ....' looks more like '"Some properties ... formal schemes" 63/64'. The source is a W-M-related reference whose exact identity is uncertain.
